what: Real 486 hardware and a real display.
why: Every DOS result comes from headless DOSBox Staging 0.83.0 with CWSDPMI. No physical 486DX, VGA card, keyboard controller or monitor has run `FIZZ2.EXE`, and nobody has looked at its mode 13h picture on a screen. The stun stars and the shot puff were grabbed from DOSBox's window under a virtual display; the death shake, a shift of at most a pixel, has not been looked at on DOS at all.

The owner heard the cluck and the Web music in playtests on 28 October 2026 and the new Web effects on 29 October 2026 (one listener, no measurement); nobody has reported hearing the DOS music, or any sound on a real AdLib, Sound Blaster or PC speaker. The DOS checks count register writes and speaker steps, the Web checks record what a stand-in `AudioContext` is asked to play, and neither can hear. The register write timings are Fizz 1's and have not been measured here.

what: Hearing the sound effects, the menu mix and the can.
why: The owner listened to the new effects on the Web on 29 October 2026 and found them good ("they sound decent", and they may revisit them), and after listening on both platforms chose Fizz 1's jump, pogo and fizz shot ("the FM versions of these render weird in DOS and they sound great in Fizz 1 DOS"); one person's statements, not measurements. That remark compares the FM versions with the original Fizz 1 DOS; nobody has reported how Fizz 2's DOS build sounds with Fizz 1 DOS's data in place, and nobody has reported listening to the music under Paused and Options (the Web low-pass at 900 Hz and 0.7 gain, and its approximation on DOS with operator levels) or to the soda can's fsssht. The Web checks record which oscillators a stand-in `AudioContext` is asked to play, and the DOS checks count register writes and speaker steps in DOSBox; neither can hear. The FM voices that remain (the alternates and the other effects) are authored by their numbers and downmixed by a best-effort mapping that was not compared by ear.

DOSBox runs `/BENCH` at a fixed 26,800 cycles a millisecond and the other checks at `cycles=max`, which hides what the `f64` rules, the drawing and the 560 Hz audio interrupt cost on a 486DX. Fizz 1's `m5/bench` and its 486 cycle estimator are the reference tools, and neither has been run against Fizz 2.

what: The Web page played by a person.
why: Headless Chromium loads the page, plays the replay's keys through the DevTools protocol and takes the screenshots. The owner played the Web build in a playtest on 28 October 2026 and found the HUD good (that was the first HUD; the Two-Row Stack has been looked at in screenshots only); the playtest notes do not cover fullscreen, Keyboard Lock, touch or a screen reader, and Firefox, Safari and a phone have not loaded the page.

what: The DOS build in a browser.
why: No js-dos or other in-browser DOS run of `FIZZ2.EXE` has been tried.

The eighteen traces are committed and Fizz 2 matches them bit for bit, but CI never runs `tools/fizz1-trace`, so nothing regenerates the files from Fizz 1 on its own. `tools/lf-sim-drift.sh` was run by hand against a Fizz 1 checkout.

what: Bundling the Web build into a launcher.
why: `dist/web` uses relative URLs so a launcher can host it under any path; no launcher has.

what: The GitHub runner, beyond the runs recorded.
why: CI passed on the head commit of each pull request and on the merge commits listed in the evidence tables ({{m.ciGreen}} merged pull requests green on main). A run not listed there has not been seen. The first full run on main after the soda can merged (#127) failed in the parallel replay of a corrupt `FIZZ2.CFG` and has not been seen to pass; no nightly run had finished when this edition was built.

what: Other DPMI hosts and DOS versions.
why: Only CWSDPMI under DOSBox's own DOS. FreeDOS, MS-DOS, EMM386 and HDPMI are untried, and the FreeDOS-bootable floppy has not been built. Whether FreeDOS's `COMMAND.COM` passes `/?` through to the program is unchecked.
